conviction_note: Q4 itself is boxed in by a tight company guide ($138-142m / $0.75-0.78) that consensus sits on, so the print turns on the first FY27 guide, where the evidence is balanced: Advantech's 1.64 book-to-bill says the industrial-edge order book is strong, while Digi's own 'order early to secure deliveries' comment and memory-cost pressure at Lantronix, Ericsson and Advantech say FY27 may be guided cautiously; with a stale, unsourced FY27 consensus every guidance finding is capped, the impact sum is +0.4 and the scaled number (p_up 53 x 9.0 abs) is +0.54, both near zero by design.

findings.finding: Advantech, the largest listed industrial edge-computing peer, reported on 2026-10-29 Q3 2026 revenue up 83% YoY / 24% QoQ to NT$32.44bn with a book-to-bill of 1.64 overall and 2.12 in North America (North America revenue +58% YoY in US$), and said 'customer ordering activity remained robust'. That is an order book running far ahead of shipments into Digi's December-quarter FY27 start, against a Digi Q4 guide that is flat sequentially ($138-142m vs Q3 $139m) and an FY27 guide the market has not seen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last first-full-year guide (2025-11-12, FY26 revenue +10-15%, EBITDA +15-20%) bought +7.12%; the guide raises on 2026-05-06 and 2026-08-05 bought +5.4% and +14.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Advantech is a Taiwan listing that Digi's US small-cap coverage does not cite; DGII fell about 4% on the 20 days after it and sits 15% below its post-August level. If the market had read a 2.12 North American book-to-bill as Digi-positive, the post-earnings drift would not still be -15%. It is still a proxy: Advantech's mix is edge AI and semiconductor equipment, not Digi's cellular routers and IoT modules.
findings.independence: Lantronix (2026-11-09) reaffirmed double-digit FY27 growth with Embedded IoT +37% (https://www.panabee.com/news/lantronix-earnings-q1-2027). Different company, different document. The Advantech release also names rising component costs, which is in the memory finding below and is not counted here.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call (2026-08-05) CEO Konezny said customers' urgency was linked to supply worries ('Boy, I better get my order in place to secure my deliveries and time lines'), and the Q3 release shows IoT Products & Services one-time sales up $12.4m YoY. Q4 is guided flat sequentially, so the first FY27 guide could build in the end of that early ordering. The 2026-11-03 Earnings Whispers preview names 'pull-forward orders' as the main risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior Digi guide that de-rated on a pull-forward unwind in the baseline window. The one negative print in 7, 2026-02-04 (-3.93%), came while management was 'battling' memory shortages (Q1 FY26 call).
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the preview names it and the stock has drifted -15% since the August beat-and-raise. What may not be priced is the size. One-time sales were the swing component of the Q3 beat (+$12.4m of the +$31m YoY), and the FY27 consensus is stale, so nobody has published what a normalised hardware base does to FY27. If it were fully priced, the whisper would not sit above the top of the Q4 guide at $0.80.
findings.independence: Inseego (2026-11-04) said carrier customers are selling units they already bought and placing smaller replenishment orders (https://www.panabee.com/news/inseego-earnings-q3-2026), a destocking read in cellular hardware, filed separately as a channel proxy. Shares no document with that finding. The Q3 release (https://www.01net.it/digi-international-reports-third-fiscal-quarter-2026-results/) gives the one-time sales split.

findings.finding: Rising memory and component costs: Digi's own Q3 release cites 'rising component costs - most notably memory', and the CFO has said the gross-margin floor is '62%, 63%' with 90-day swings of '200, 300 basis points' against a record 64.8% in Q3. Since Digi last spoke, three peers have flagged the same pressure: Advantech (2026-10-29, a 'temporary year-over-year decline in gross margin' from component costs), Ericsson (2026-10-15, enterprise wireless facing higher component costs) and Lantronix (2026-11-09, inventory built against extended memory lead times). That puts the FY27 EBITDA-margin guide at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has surprised up for four quarters (Q3 adj. EBITDA margin 29.1%, +47% YoY) and each print was bought; the February print, when memory was the call's main topic, fell 3.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: The pressure itself is public. What is not priced is the FY27 margin guide, because no current FY27 EBITDA consensus exists. Digi has offset costs through pricing and recurring revenue so far, and the Q4 EBITDA guide ($40-41.5m) is flat-to-up on Q3 despite the warning. If the market expected margin compression, the Q4 whisper would not be above guide.
findings.independence: Ericsson Q3 (https://lightreading.com/finance/ericsson-disbands-wireless-enterprise-biz-as-higher-component-costs-loom, 2026-10-15) and Advantech Q3 (https://www.advantech.com/zh-tw/resources/news/advantech-reports-3q26-eps-of-nt715) are separate documents pointing the same way. The Lantronix gross-margin threshold of 45% comes from Panabee's AI-generated risk list, not from management. Peplink raised prices on 11 models citing memory costs from 2026-06-01 (https://5gstore.com/blog/2026/04/27/peplink-price-increases-june-2026/), which suggests pricing pass-through is available to router vendors.

findings.finding: ARR was $191m at Q3 against a year-end guide of at least 27% growth (about $193m on FY25's $152m), and the long-term target is $200m ARR and $200m adj. EBITDA by fiscal 2028. The 2026-11-03 Earnings Whispers preview says the ARR target 'could arrive ahead of schedule', so the Q4 call is the natural place to hit or reset the long-term target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ARR guide went from ~10% (Nov 2025) to 25% (May 2026) to at least 27% (Aug 2026), and both raises were bought (+5.4%, +14.1%).
findings.why_not_priced: The ARR print itself is inside the company's own guide, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect and is sized near zero. The unpriced part is a new long-term target, which is speculative: management has given no date for one. If a reset were priced, the stock would not trade 20% below its high at a 24.9x forward P/E.
findings.independence: Q3 release ARR figures (https://www.01net.it/digi-international-reports-third-fiscal-quarter-2026-results/), the same company data. Particle drives IoT P&S ARR +100%, and its acquisition anniversary in Jan 2027 removes the inorganic boost to FY27 ARR growth.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-27 Digi replaced its $250m revolver with a $350m senior secured revolver maturing 2031: lower pricing (SOFR +125-262.5bp vs 135-310bp) and an accordion, with stated use 'future permitted acquisitions'. Net debt was $81m at Q3 against roughly $146m of FY26 adj. EBITDA, so capacity for another ARR acquisition exists.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Digi's acquisition cadence (Ventus Nov 2023, Jolt Aug 2025, Particle Jan 2026) has been followed by ARR-led guide raises that were bought. No acquisition was announced on the print day in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility is public and priced. The only unpriced element is whether a deal is disclosed with results, and nothing dated says one is. Asked what the money buys: acquisitions, consistent with a two-deal record in 12 months, with leverage under 1x. So the sign is positive or zero, not distress.
findings.independence: Company press release of 2026-08-31 (same event). Nothing independent points to a pending deal.

findings.finding: Expectations into the print have been reset by price, not by estimates. The stock is -15.4% since the 08-05 beat-and-raise (Earnings Whispers), -10.6% from 8/5 to 11/10 against SPY -2.6% (AAII), and -5.8% over the last 5 sessions. Meanwhile estimate revisions are 1 up and 0 down over the last month, the Q4 consensus ($0.76) sits mid-guide, Digi has beaten EPS by 9.8-16.7% in each of the last four quarters (Benzinga), and 6 of the last 7 prints rose.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: +14.1, +5.4, -3.93, +7.12, +0.47, +14.07, +17.33. Beats have been bought, median |move| 7.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a positioning read, not a fact the market lacks. The drawdown has no single dated cause found (no 8-K, no downgrade dated Oct-Nov 2026; the Craig-Hallum downgrade on Quantisnow is dated 2024-11-14), so it is sized small. It counts as a setup because estimates did not fall with the price: if the market expected a miss, revisions would be negative.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers PEAD -15.4% and whisper $0.80 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/dgii); Benzinga beat history (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DGII/earnings-forecasts). Separate aggregators of the same tape.

findings.finding: Lantronix, a direct embedded/industrial IoT peer, reported on 2026-11-09 fiscal Q1 FY27 revenue of $32.4m (+8.6% YoY) inside its $31-33m guide, Embedded IoT +37%, a Q2 guide of $32.5-34.5m (up sequentially) and reaffirmed double-digit FY27 growth. That is the most recent IoT hardware read and it shows no demand break.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of DGII reacting to Lantronix prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. It landed two days before Digi and after Digi last spoke, and DGII still fell over the week, so it has not lifted the name. Panabee is AI-generated and was not verified against Lantronix's 8-K.
findings.independence: Advantech's order data points the same way (filed above, separate document).

findings.finding: Inseego (2026-11-04) cut its Q4 outlook for its North America business ($21-25m) because carrier customers are working down units already bought and placing smaller replenishment orders, and it delayed a product launch to Q1 2027 on extended printed-circuit-board lead times. That is a destocking and lead-time read in cellular hardware.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of DGII reacting to Inseego prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Inseego sells carrier FWA and mobile hotspots, while Digi sells enterprise and industrial routers and modules through distribution, so the transmission is weak and the market likely treats it as idiosyncratic to Inseego. That is why it is sized small; it is a channel proxy, not a Digi number.
findings.independence: Inseego 8-K exhibit 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022652/000168316826008301/inseego_ex9901.htm). Pull-forward commentary at Arrow points loosely the same way. Shares no document with the Digi pull-forward finding.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with (unusable chain). The findings are net slightly positive against a negative 5d/20d run-up and a -15% post-earnings drift, which cuts against the tape. That is why p_up sits at 53 rather than the 6-of-7 up base rate.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): FY27 consensus is unsourced and stale, so the guidance findings were capped. Advantech went +1.0 to +0.7, pull-forward -1.0 to -0.7, memory -0.8 to -0.6 (also a proxy, lesson 5), and the ARR target +0.5 to +0.4 (its ARR print is inside the company's own guide).
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not a cause): the positioning finding went from +0.8 to +0.4 because no dated cause for the drawdown was found.
Lesson 5 (proxy): Inseego, a different channel, went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing): asked what the money buys. The answer is acquisitions, at leverage under 1x and consistent with the Jolt and Particle record, so the sign stays +0.2.
Lesson 1 (reaction): this name has bought beats (6 of 7 up), so no veto on the reaction; abs_move_pct 9.0 and p_up 53 unchanged.
Net: impact_sum went from +0.6 to +0.4; expected_move_pct is unchanged at +0.54.
